genre: Sports / Kabaddi: raid-and-tackle duels with asynchronous ghost PvP, team-builder auction and league career
title: Kabaddi Ghost Raids: Raid League
audience: Kabaddi fans in India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Iran and the diaspora. Competitive mobile players aged 13+ who want a real kabaddi game with real rules. Friend groups who trade ghost codes and chase weekly ladder bragging rights. Cricket-auction-league players who enjoy squad building.
controls:
RAID (touch only):
- Drag a path from the raider across the mat. Lines show reach range and the defenders' danger zones.
- Move-buttons appear contextually as thumb-reachable arcs: Hand Touch (tap near a defender), Toe Touch (flick down at a defender's feet), Dubki (swipe down under a reach, then back up), Dash (double-tap forward, burst through a gap), Backward Kick (flick backward while a defender is behind), Escape (see Struggle).
- A bonus-line hop is a tap while crossing the bonus line, valid only with 6 or more defenders.
- Raid timer is a 30 s ring. Return crossing the midline by swipe-back or auto-run-home on a held tap.
- Cant-be-caught-once-crossed rule: the player may still cross the midline while a tackle is incomplete (the hold meter is under 100%).

STRUGGLE: when held, a tug-of-war mini-game. Rhythmic taps fill the escape ring while the hold-ring drains. Swipe toward the midline for a lunge. Pull-away timing windows give a perfect-escape bonus. A fresher raider with high Stamina gets a wider window.

DEFENSE (during the opponent's raid, never automatic):
- Tap a defender to select or switch (a radial highlight, instant switch with no delay). The player may also drag the selected defender to shift position, and the AI raider reacts.
- Tackle timing: a shrinking ring around the raider, with the tackle button tied to the selected defender. Success depends on distance, angle, the defender's skill, and timing. Ankle Hold: tap when the ring is on the legs. Thigh Hold: tap-and-hold. Chain Tackle: tap a second adjacent defender within the chain window. Dash: swipe toward the raider for a rush. Block: hold to form a wall.
- Miss rate is measurable and tested. Target: a median player lands about 55-60% of single tackles and about 70% of correct chain tackles. A tap at the wrong time or from the wrong position fails, and the raider can score or get a bonus.

SETTINGS: vibration on/off with intensity, sound/music/commentary volume sliders, left-handed mirror, raider choice for each raid, colour-blind marks, and reduced motion.
core_loop:
Micro-loop (30-60 s): Read the formation, then drag a raid path and pick a move. Touch defenders, return across the midline, and the referee panel shows the points. Then switch sides and defend with timed tackles. In the Ghost mode, the raid is recorded as a compact input trace (path points, move calls, timings).

Session loop (5-8 min): Play a Quick Match, a Tournament round or a campaign Raid Trial. Earn coins, Chant Tokens, form XP and trophies. Do the daily Ghost Challenge, set the defense Ghost Gate, and collect the ghost-raid results from friends and ladder players, who attacked your gate while you were away.

Meta loop (daily/weekly): Build the squad through the auction and the team-builder, upgrade player skills and stamina, and unlock jerseys, mat designs and chants. Climb the weekly ladder under the weekly formation theme. Win a Tournament to unlock a Championship. Complete season cups and fill the Kit Album.

Async design: ghosts are deterministic replays of an input trace resolved by a shared simulation, so there is no network lag during play. Online head-to-head quick match is turn-based (raid, then defend) with 20 s turns. Every online mode has an AI fallback.

positioning: 'The kabaddi game done right': official-style rules, 6 raid moves, 5 defense moves, real struggle mini-games, active AI on three difficulties, an auction, commentary in Hindi and English, and lag-free ghost PvP with friends. Rewarded-only ads and a one-time Remove Ads. Honest store creatives that only show real gameplay (answering the fake-ad backlash).
progression:
PLAYER RANK: Raider Rank 1-60 from XP (matches, trials, ghosts). It unlocks mat designs, chants, jersey slots and Ghost Gate slots.

SQUAD: build a 12-player squad, 7 on the mat and 5 subs. Each player has 5 skills (Raid Reach, Tackle Grip, Speed, Stamina, Agility) and a role. Players level via training and match-form XP. Upgrades cost coins and time-free training points (no waiting-timer paywalls). Players have a fatigue/form meter rewarding rotation.

AUCTION and TEAM BUILDER: a seasonal player auction against AI franchises with a budget (the 'purse'), where bids are played in real time against AI bidders. It's all in-game currency. No real-money randomness, and players are fully visible with their stats. Real-style fictional teams and players (original names, e.g. 'Jaipur Jaguars'-style invented franchises, no real PKL names or logos). The licensed-content hooks are designed so a license can be dropped in later after legal review.

KIT ALBUM (collection): jerseys, mats, banners, chants, celebration animations, and referee gestures. Completing sets unlocks a bonus cosmetic. Cosmetic chants (crowd chants and drum patterns) can be equipped for your Ghost Gate.

SEASONS and LADDERS: 4-week seasons, weekly ghost ladder with divisions (Bronze to Legend), weekly formation theme (e.g. 'Cage', 'Pincer', 'Diamond', 'Wall') that changes the defender layout. Weekly rewards by division, plus season trophies.

DAILY: Daily Ghost Challenge (beat a curated ghost), Daily Drill (3 raids), login streak (7-day with a cosmetic at day 7, a streak freeze earned by play), and daily chest.

LIVE ROADMAP: an in-app 'Roadmap' screen shows what's coming (new languages, tournaments, teams, DRS upgrades), supports a vote among 3 options and an update-notes inbox.

COMMENTARY: English and Hindi at launch; Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Punjabi and Marathi are added via the roadmap (text subtitles at launch, with voice packs as optional downloads).

sample_levels.objective: Learn the raid: drag a path and hand-touch one defender, then return across the midline.
sample_levels.win_condition: Score 1 touch point and return safely.
lose_conditions: Held by the defender without escaping

sample_levels.objective: Defend: stop the opposing raider using a timed ankle hold on the tackle ring.
The grip is tight: break out of a hold with the struggle mini-game, then touch two defenders.
sample_levels.win_condition: Escape at least once and score 3 points.

sample_levels.objective: Defenders reach high: slip under with a Dubki and toe touch the corner.
sample_levels.win_condition: Score 3 points with at least one Dubki or Toe Touch.

sample_levels.objective: Two empty raids already. Win the Do-or-Die raid or you are out.
sample_levels.win_condition: Score at least 1 point on the Do-or-Die raid.
lose_conditions: Raider is out on the Do-or-Die raid

sample_levels.objective: Breather: a relaxed match with six defenders on the mat. Hop the bonus line for an easy lead.
sample_levels.win_condition: Earn 1 bonus point and win by 4.

sample_levels.objective: You are down 2 players. Time a Backward Kick on the chasing defender to turn the raid.
sample_levels.win_condition: Score with a Backward Kick and keep the team at 5 or more players.

sample_levels.objective: All out at minute 5 of the half. Play on: win raids to revive teammates and finish the half.
sample_levels.win_condition: Survive to the 20:00 mark and trail by no more than 2 points with the full side revived.

sample_levels.objective: Build the squad: win three auction lots within the purse and play the first league match.
sample_levels.win_condition: Buy at least 1 Raider, 1 Corner and 1 Anchor, then win the match.

sample_levels.objective: Three defenders left. Defend the Super Raid threat with a chain tackle.
sample_levels.win_condition: Land a chain tackle (Super Tackle, 2 points).

sample_levels.objective: Ghost Duel: beat a weekly-theme ghost's 'Cage' formation, and review the touch with DRS.
sample_levels.win_condition: Beat the ghost's score and win one DRS review.

sample_levels.objective: World Final on Hard: a full 2x20 game-clock match against the rival captain, all moves in play.
sample_levels.win_condition: Finish ahead on points after both halves, with revivals and the Do-or-Die rule in force.

level_structure:
CONTENT UNITS: 66 handcrafted Raid Trials in a 6-chapter campaign, each a short match scenario (a half-match segment or a scored situation, 2-6 real minutes), plus 6 chapter-end Full Matches (the full-length 2x20 game-clock halves). Total 66 units plus the 6 full matches.

Match clock: official-style 20-minute halves in game time. Real time is compressed with a clock scale of 5x (a half takes about 4 minutes real time, a Full Match about 9-10 minutes with half-time). Quick Match offers 'Full (2x20)' and a Blitz option (2x10 game-time). A QA hook can set the clock to jump to minute 5 and force an all-out.

RULES ENGINE (single source of truth feeding the scoreboard and referee animations):
- 7 players per side. Touch points, bonus point (needs 6 or more defenders on the mat), tackle point, super tackle (3 or fewer defenders is 2 pts), super raid (3 or more touches in one raid), all-out (+2) followed by revival (one player back per point earned), Do-or-Die raid on the third consecutive empty raid, a 30 s raid clock, and the half time swap.
- An all-out never ends the half. Players are revived per point and the clock keeps running. The referee panel and scoreboard come from the same event object, so points always match. Automated tests cover multi-point raids.

CHAPTER 1: VILLAGE MAT (Trials 1-11, tutorial warm-up). Introduces: Hand Touch, Dash, defender timing, a single-ring tackle, the struggle mini-game. Aha: read the gap, not the defender. Trial 11 is Full Match: Village Final.
CHAPTER 2: DISTRICT CUP (12-22). Introduces: Toe Touch, Dubki, the empty-raid counter and Do-or-Die, the bonus line. Aha: dubki under a reach. Trial 22 is Full Match with a Do-or-Die finish.
CHAPTER 3: STATE LEAGUE (23-33). Introduces: Backward Kick, Escape from holds, Super Tackle, all-out and revival. Aha: sacrificing a raid to win a revival. Trial 33 is Full Match with a comeback.
CHAPTER 4: AUCTION SEASON (34-44). Introduces: the auction and squad builder, player roles (Raider, Left/Right Corner, Cover, Anchor), Ankle and Thigh Hold specialists, switching defenders. Aha: matching your hold to a raider's style. Trial 44 is Full Match, your own auctioned squad.
CHAPTER 5: CONTINENTAL CUP (45-55). Introduces: Super Raid, Chain Tackles, DRS review challenges, formation themes (Ghost Gate). Aha: two defenders, one chain. Trial 55 is Full Match semi-final.
CHAPTER 6: WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP (56-66). Introduces: a combination of everything, rival captains with signature traits, endurance with fatigue. Trial 66 is the World Final Full Match, played on Hard.

EACH CHAPTER pacing: 3 intro trials, 3 twist trials, 2 combine trials, 1 breather (a lower-pressure scored trial, 3 stars easy), 1 spike (a tight scenario), 1 chapter boss (Full Match).

TRIAL TYPES: Raid Puzzle (score N with a given formation), Defend Stand (stop the raider X times), Comeback (win from a deficit), Do-or-Die Drill, Revival Run (survive an all-out), Super Challenge (earn a super tackle or raid), Ghost Duel (beat a ghost's trace).

STARS: 3 stars per trial (win, clean play such as no empty raids or tackle accuracy, perfect timing or a target margin). Stars unlock chapter chests and the next chapters' trophy gate.

MODE GATES (all playable or showing requirements and progress):
- Quick Match: open on the first launch (vs. AI, 3 difficulties).
- Tournament: unlocks after 1 completed match. The lock card shows 'Complete 1 match (0/1)'.
- Championship: unlocks after a Tournament win. The lock card shows 'Win 1 Tournament (0/1)'.
- Ghost Ladder: unlocks after campaign Trial 5 with a progress counter.
- Auction: unlocks at Chapter 4 start, or earlier via Team Builder. It shows 'Reach Trial 34 (n/34)'. The basic team builder is open from the start.
difficulty_curve:
Rated 0-1 per trial. Ch1: 0.10 to 0.35 with a breather at trial 8 (0.18) and a first spike at trial 10 (0.42). Ch2: 0.30 to 0.50, with a spike at trial 20 (a Do-or-Die with a 1-point margin, 0.60) then a breather at trial 21 (0.35). Ch3: 0.40 to 0.60, a revival spike at trial 31 (0.68), a breather at 32. Ch4: 0.45 to 0.65 with the first squad-dependent spike at trial 42 (0.72). Ch5: 0.55 to 0.75 and the first chain-timing spike at trial 53 (0.80). Ch6: 0.65 to 0.90, final boss at 0.92.

AI DIFFICULTY (all three levels attack actively): 
- Easy: the CPU raids every possession, scoring on roughly 35% of its raids. It makes a mistake with a 40% rate and has a wide tackle window for the player.
- Medium: roughly 45% raid success, a mixed move set, with chain tackles used.
- Hard: roughly 55-60% raid success. Smarter defender switching and multi-defender chains, bluff raids and Do-or-Die awareness. Target: the CPU wins at least 40% of matches against average players, validated by telemetry and auto-play bots in QA.
- Adaptive: a quiet assist after 3 straight losses (slightly wider windows, never visible as free wins) and a stretch after 5 wins. Players can always change difficulty manually.
- No free tackles: the AI raider moves independently of the player's choices.
camera_orientation: Landscape, 2.5D side-on mat view. Skia-rendered layered 2D skeletal rigs with parallax crowd and stands. The camera does a slow pan and zoom on raids and a punch-in on touches and tackles. Menus, the auction and ghost lab are landscape too, with a one-thumb reachable layout. Rigs are authored from motion-reference captures, so no 3D is required (2D-only studio rule). Tuned for 60 fps on mid-range devices with a Low graphics toggle.
market_opportunity: Kabaddi is a huge audience in South Asia (a PKL following of hundreds of millions), but the Play Store offers few kabaddi games, and the top ones are criticised for poor graphics, shallow defense, passive AI, locked modes and heavy ads. Search interest for 'kabaddi game', 'kabaddi multiplayer game' and 'kabaddi raid' is strong, and the best result (Le Panga) sits at roughly 1M installs. An async ghost format avoids the lag complaints of live PvP, supports viral friend codes and gives season-long retention. Authentic rules plus real depth plus light ads fills the gap.
competitor_contrast: Versus Le Panga: Kabaddi Game and other kabaddi apps: deeper raid and defense (they have a single tackler or a yellow diamond tap), real rules (revivals, Do-or-Die, bonus line, super tackle), active AI with difficulty levels, open Tournament and Championship modes with clear unlock rules, stronger art and animation, a team-builder/auction, ghost-based online play without lag, and far fewer ads. Versus Clash Royale-type PvP: no real-time netcode, so it runs on bad connections.
economy_monetization:
CURRENCIES: Coins (soft: from matches, trials, daily), Auction Purse (per-season, non-purchasable, earned by play) and Chant Tokens (cosmetic unlock currency from albums and ladder), plus Gems (a premium currency used only for cosmetics, bought by IAP or earned slowly). There are NO loot boxes or random paid rewards: every cosmetic shows exactly what it is.

ADS (rewarded-first, designed around the player research):
- Rewarded video only at launch: double match coins, a retry of a failed trial, an extra training point, a free daily cosmetic spin-free reveal (a fixed item, not random). All optional, with the reward clearly stated.
- Interstitial (after launch, capped): at most 1 per match, placed only at half time or match end or in menus. None in the first 2 completed matches, none during live gameplay, none within 5 s of a score, none on app launch, none after every raid. Skippable after 5 s.
- Offline: the whole game, including campaign, quick match vs. AI, and squad builder, works offline. Ghost ladders sync when online, data usage is light, and ad SDKs are lazy-loaded, with a single lightweight mediation.

IAP: Remove Ads (one-time, removes interstitials; keeps optional rewarded boosts), cosmetic jersey/mat/chant packs, Team Packs (fixed, visible fictional franchise kit sets), a Season Pass (cosmetic track plus extra Album slots, no match advantage), and a Starter Bundle (cosmetics plus Remove Ads discount).

FAIRNESS: no pay-to-win. Cosmetics only affect looks, and training boosts never carry a purchasable stat advantage over free ones in ladders. Ghost Ladder matches use normalised stat caps per division.
technical_assumptions: React Native with Skia for the mat and Reanimated for animations and the UI. 2D layered skeletal rigs (a 2.5D look). The research asks for 3D mocap players, but the studio rule is 2D-only for now, so quality is pursued through high-fidelity rigged 2D animation, reviewed as a commercial risk (review_flag: true on graphics expectations).

Deterministic fixed-step match simulation (60 Hz) shared by the client and a server validator, with a seeded RNG. Ghosts are stored as compact input traces (about 1-3 KB) plus the seed, formation id and version.

Anti-cheat: the server re-simulates every uploaded ghost and rejects mismatches, uses signed submissions, rate limits, plausibility checks on timings and reach, and a flag-and-shadow-ban pipeline for outliers. Review flag: anti-cheat risk on ghost data.

Async ghosts are resolved locally against a downloaded trace, so there is zero live netcode lag. Online duels are turn-based with a 20 s turn limit and an AI takeover on disconnect. Every online mode has an AI fallback.
Backend: a lightweight service (Supabase or Firebase) for ladders, friend room codes, ghost storage, and the season config. Generated names, a fixed set of 8 emotes, no chat and no typed text.
Offline-first: the campaign, quick match, tournament and squad builder work without network, and the ladder syncs when connected.
The rules engine is a single event-based module that drives both the scoreboard and the referee animations (one source of truth).
Time scale: the 20-minute game-clock halves run at a 5x clock scale; the QA time-skip hook sets the clock to minute 5.
Target 60 fps on mid-range Android (4 GB RAM). Graphics presets: Low (smaller atlases, fewer crowd layers, build under about 150 MB with on-demand asset and voice pack downloads), Medium and High.
Commentary: audio packs per language, downloaded on demand. Hindi and English at launch.
Licensing: no real PKL names, logos or players at launch (original, real-style content), with a clear data layer so licensed packs can be added after legal review. Review flag: licensing.

Ads: rewarded-first through a single lightweight mediation SDK, loaded lazily, a frequency cap managed by an ad-gate service (no interstitial in the first 2 matches, none during play or within 5 s of a score).
Privacy: consent flows for ads and analytics, a child-safe configuration, no personal data in ghosts or names.
Store creatives must show only real in-game footage.
qa_acceptance_criteria: First-session flow: Quick Match, Tournament and Championship are all visible. Tournament shows 'Complete 1 match (0/1)' and unlocks after 1 completed match. Championship shows 'Win 1 Tournament (0/1)' and unlocks after a Tournament win. No permanently locked menu item exists.
Simulating an all-out at game-clock minute 5 does not end the half: revivals apply and play continues to 20:00. The half lasts the full 20 game minutes.

Do-or-Die triggers on the third consecutive empty raid. The bonus point is never awarded with fewer than 6 defenders. A super tackle is awarded with 3 or fewer defenders. A super raid triggers with 3 or more touches.
The referee panel animation and the scoreboard come from one event: an automated test over multi-point raids, tackles, bonus, all-out and revival shows zero mismatches over 1000 simulated matches.

6 raid moves (Hand Touch, Toe Touch, Dubki, Dash, Backward Kick, Escape) and 5 defender moves (Ankle Hold, Thigh Hold, Chain Tackle, Dash, Block) are implemented, each with a unique animation, plus a struggle mini-game when held.

Defense is never automatic: the measured tackle miss rate with random-timing input is at least 30%, and a tackle from a bad position or with bad timing fails. Chain tackles require 2 or more defenders and correct timing.
The player can select and switch defenders during the opponent's raid with a response under 100 ms, and can cross the midline while a tackle is incomplete.

AI: in 1000 bot-vs-AI matches the opposing raider attempts a raid every possession, scores on at least 25% of raids at Easy, and the Hard CPU wins at least 40% of matches against an average-skill bot.

Ads: no ad on launch before play, no interstitial in the first 2 completed matches, none during live play, none within 5 s of a score, and at most 1 interstitial per match at half time or match end. Rewarded ads are always optional. Remove Ads removes all interstitials and persists across reinstalls.
Vibration and sound (music, effects, commentary) can each be turned off and stay off after restart.

The ghost pipeline works: recording a raid, uploading, server re-simulation, and replaying it as a defender gives identical results. A tampered ghost is rejected. Ghost play has no network dependency during the match.
Online: quick match, friend rooms by 6-character code and the weekly ladder work. An AI fallback exists for every online mode, only the 8 fixed emotes exist, and there is no chat or typed text.

Performance: 60 fps on a mid-range reference Android device on Medium graphics, with no frame below 45 fps in a 10-minute match. The Low preset install is under about 150 MB, and voice packs download on demand.
The auction, team builder, jersey customiser, raider selection and replay/DRS review all work offline or degrade gracefully.
English and Hindi commentary play and match the on-screen events. Missing languages show subtitles only.
The campaign has 66 trials across 6 chapters plus 6 full matches, each with 3 star goals, and every mechanic is introduced in its stated chapter.
The in-app roadmap screen is reachable from the home hub and settings.
Content rating: Everyone, no blood, no gambling, no loot boxes (the auction uses only in-game currency, with visible stats), no chat, and the store listing uses only real gameplay footage.
